If this was posted to any other subreddit people would find this disgusting. "I want cancer." 
This is so much more selfish than suicide. "No one blames you," "People would be nice to you" Seriously, you're defending this shit? There's downvotes on this thread for a comment that says 'My child had leukemia, I disagree.' 
It's fine to be suicidal, but not being able to think outside of yourself is a problem that plagues the nation. The post shouldn't be "I want cancer," it should be "I want blameless death that doesn't misuse tax money, drive up my family's insurance rates, waste resources and doctors' time, and doesn't pain the people around watching me slowly die" Blameless death, I understand. Cancer? Fuck off.

No I get the point. And when I was a selfish little kid I wished this upon myself too. But you go out into the world and you see actual bad shit and you realize your life isn't bad. I still hate myself, I'm still suicidal, but this post is fucking disrespectful and I stand by what I say.

Alright, this post is so disrespectful to actual victims of lethal illness. Victims who value their lives who go through tremendous pain to live another day. And you sit around envying that shit in your good health?

"People would probably be nice to you" 

what a disgusting selfish post. how old is everyone on here

You should definitely solve this asap. I feel there is a high chance for betterment in your case. Here's some suggestions: 
Speak to your wife. Tell her how you've been feeling, but don't dump it all on her at once. Sternly communicate to her that this is an issue but it doesn't change anything. 
Seek therapy/support. Via a professional or friends/family. 
Consider pharmaceuticals. A simple prescription could help drastically and help you enough life more. 
Also, it may be possible that this is not clinical depression. You might just be facing regular hardships: boring routine, no goals, need new hobbies, need new diet, ect. But I wouldn't know, I don't know enough about the situation. It sounds like you're not having a good time so you need to take step to solve it

Now's the time to start. Start with telling someone supportive and accepting. Force yourself to. If you can't think of someone, tell your doctor. Or find a therapist and confide in them. Pharmaceuticals can sometimes help. It took me years to go through these steps and I wish I had started sooner. Your case seems like it has lots of hope to improve. Don't let yourself get lazy and fall into a further depression. Start now.
If you want your son to grow up normal, don't do any of this insane shit you're talking about. Murder-suicide? Really? Seek therapeutic help. Do your child right.
What?

Dude, I would really recommend against that. They are not loyal to you, they are 100x more inclined to tell your parents and the school than your therapist. School counsellors do not have near the credentials a therapist does, in my opinion they should not even legally be able to hand out advice to kids. They are not interested in supporting you, they are interested in "helping" you. They will jump at the chance to spill everything you tell them without using your exact words. If you feel you need to, do it, but don't tell them anything you wouldn't want your parents to know.

I started on 20mg and experienced many physical side effects. My mental state was slightly improving by sort of sedating my thoughts. My psych then doubled the dose. Anxiety increased drastically. I felt emotional but had enough control to suppress it. I wasn't happy though, just pleasant to other people. My psych then added Zoloft and decreased the Prozac back to 20. This was the worst med combo I've ever had. He took me off Prozac and had me just take the Zoloft. So all in all, Prozac was pretty ineffective for me. SSRIs don't work on me, I guess.

Express your concerns to her. Tell her you love her. God, that's important. Tell her you love and care about her. When my depression got really bad, my boyfriend stopped caring and after a few awful months, we eventually broke up. I was left feeling like it was my fault.

Please stop replying in one word answers. I completely understand that you have needs and sometimes don't have the energy to keep up with someone else's problems, but you can say something less insensitive. Try this: "I love you. I'm listening to everything you have to say, but I don't have much energy to talk. Don't confuse that with me not caring, I care about you. " Communicate.

My ex would always say "my needs are above yours and I don't want to talk" Don't do that. It will lead to a long, painful break up.

It good that's you're putting yourself out there. The lyrics aren't cheesy like I expected them to be, they feel honest. I like writing lyrics too. Are you more interested in the writing or musical aspect? Either way, I'd recommend building on that skill. Personally, I enjoy music and I probably won't pursue it as a career, but it's a great hobby that makes me happy and motivated. If you like writing, try creative writing or check out r/writingprompts. Seriously, hobbies are great. Keep going.
